description: Figure 6(b) is a line plot that illustrates the impact of the hyperparameter $N$ on the Area Under the Curve (AUC) score. The x-axis, labeled with the variable $N$, ranges from 0 to 20 with a step of 5, and is marked with the values 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis, labeled "AUC", ranges from 0.7 to 1.0 with a step of 0.1. The plot displays five distinct lines, each representing a different method: SMD (orange, square markers), PSM (blue, circle markers), SWaT (green, star markers), SMAP (purple, diamond markers), and MSI (yellow, diamond markers). The SMD method shows a steady increase in AUC from approximately 0.75 at $N=0$ to a peak of about 0.92 at $N=10$, after which it slightly declines to around 0.90 at $N=20$. The PSM method starts at an AUC of about 0.95, increases to a peak of approximately 0.97 at $N=10$, and then decreases to about 0.94 at $N=20$. The SWaT method begins at an AUC of about 0.85, rises to a peak of approximately 0.91 at $N=10$, and then decreases to about 0.88 at $N=20$. The SMAP method starts at an AUC of about 0.72, increases to a peak of approximately 0.92 at $N=10$, and then decreases to about 0.85 at $N=20$. The MSI method starts at an AUC of about 0.80, increases to a peak of approximately 0.90 at $N=10$, and then decreases to about 0.85 at $N=20$.
